LT:CharacterLiteral.Definition: A {c:bold}character{/c} literal represents a single Unicode character enclosed in single quotes, such as {c:code}'A'{/c} or {c:code}'\n'{/c}.

LT:QuotedString.Definition: A {c:bold}quoted{/c} string literal represents a sequence of characters enclosed in double quotes. It must fit on a single line.<break/>Escape sequences such as {c:code}\n{/c} (newline) and {c:code}\t{/c} (tab) can be used to include special characters.

LT:VerbatimString.Definition: A {c:bold}verbatim{/c} string literal uses the {c:color-orange keyword}@{/c} prefix and treats every character as literal — backslashes are not processed as escape sequences. Verbatim strings can span multiple lines.<break/>To include a double-quote inside a verbatim string, write it as {c:code}""{/c}.

LT:InterpolatedString.Definition: An {c:bold}interpolated{/c} string literal uses the {c:color-orange keyword}${/c} prefix and allows expressions to be embedded directly in the text by enclosing them in braces. It must fit on a single line.<break/>Escape sequences like {c:code}\n{/c} and {c:code}\t{/c} are supported, and to include a literal brace write {c:code}{{{/c} or {c:code}}}{/c}.

LT:InterpolatedVerbatimString.Definition: An {c:bold}interpolated verbatim{/c} string literal combines interpolation and verbatim behavior. It uses either the {c:color-orange keyword}$@{/c} or {c:color-orange keyword}@${/c} prefix, can span multiple lines, and does not process escape sequences.<break/>To include a double-quote write {c:code}""{/c}, and to include a literal brace write {c:code}{{{/c} or {c:code}}}{/c}.

LT:DecimalLiteral.Definition: A {c:bold}decimal{/c} literal is a numeric value written with the {c:color-light-green keyword}m{/c} suffix, specifying the {c:color-blue keyword}decimal{/c} type. Decimal is a 128-bit high-precision type commonly used for financial and monetary calculations.

LT:FloatingPointLiteral.Definition: A {c:bold}floating-point{/c} literal is a numeric value written with the {c:color-light-green keyword}f{/c} suffix, specifying the {c:color-blue keyword}float{/c} type. Float is a 32-bit single-precision type with less precision than {c:color-blue keyword}double{/c}.

LT:NumericLiteral.Definition: A {c:bold}numeric{/c} literal is an integer value written directly in code.<break/>Integer literals can be written in decimal, hexadecimal ({c:code}0x{/c} prefix), or binary ({c:code}0b{/c} prefix) notation.
